issues.legal_issue: A distinct, expedited procedure for correcting revenue records during a compulsory consolidation scheme does not deny equal protection when it provides notice, an opportunity to object and present evidence, and an appeal, and the procedural distinction is reasonably connected to the scheme’s purpose.
material_facts: The challenged procedure applied to villages undergoing consolidation, unlike the procedure for other villages under the general revenue law.
The consolidation officer gave affected persons notice of proposed corrections, heard objections, and allowed them to present evidence.
An appeal was available from the initial correction order.
The petitioners objected that the consolidation procedure differed from the ordinary revenue procedure and barred recourse to civil and revenue courts.
The consolidation scheme was intended to combine scattered plots into compact holdings and was considered to require completion within a reasonable time.
issues.conclusion: The procedure under Chapter II, read with the rules, did not violate Article 14; the challenge to it failed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits a procedural classification based on an intelligible differentia reasonably connected to the legislation’s objective. In the circumstances of consolidation, an expeditious procedure is justified if it is not arbitrary or lacking in the essentials of natural justice. The Court relied on sections 7 to 12 and 49 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, the applicable rules, and the contrast with the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901. No earlier judicial decisions were relied upon for this ruling.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and (affected_persons_receive_notice and affected_persons_can_present_objections_and_evidence and appeal_is_available) and procedure_is_designed_for_timely_completion and procedural_distinction_advances_consolidation_objective

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The challenged procedure is used in a proceeding to consolidate agricultural holdings.
predicates.affected_persons_receive_notice: The authority gives notice of proposed record corrections to persons affected by them.
predicates.affected_persons_can_present_objections_: Affected persons may object to the proposed corrections, be heard, and present evidence.
predicates.appeal_is_available: A person aggrieved by the initial correction order may appeal it.
predicates.procedure_is_designed_for_timely_complet: The procedure is structured to complete the consolidation proceeding within a reasonable time.
predicates.procedural_distinction_advances_consolid: The different procedure is reasonably connected to completing consolidation and achieving its agricultural benefits.

issues.definition: When a consolidation proceeding uses a timely procedure that advances consolidation’s objective while giving affected persons notice, an opportunity to object and present evidence, and an appeal, the record-correction procedure does not violate equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: Expedited procedures for settling principles and proposals in a consolidation scheme, including making an arbitrator’s title decision final and staying related court proceedings, do not deny equal protection when the procedures are reasonably connected to completing consolidation in a reasonable time.
material_facts: The Act provided for publication of statements of principles and proposals, invited objections, and provided for hearings and decisions by consolidation officers.
Disputed questions of title could be referred through a civil judge to an arbitrator, who heard the parties and received oral and documentary evidence.
The arbitrator’s decision was final, and proceedings concerning title to the same land in ordinary courts were stayed.
The petitioners objected that the provisions limited ordinary court jurisdiction and differed from the protections available to tenure-holders outside consolidation.
The procedures were intended to avoid delays that could prevent completion of the consolidation scheme.
issues.conclusion: The provisions of Chapter III did not violate Article 14; the challenge to them failed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits a classification with a rational basis and a nexus to the legislation’s objective. The need to complete consolidation within a reasonable time can justify procedures that limit ordinary appeals and court proceedings, including final arbitration of title disputes. The Court relied on sections 14 to 22 and 49 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act and the applicable rules. No earlier judicial decisions were relied upon for this ruling.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and objections_to_principles_and_proposals_are_heard and title_disputes_receive_a_hearing_and_evidence and finality_and_stays_prevent_delay and procedural_limits_advance_consolidation_objective

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The challenged procedure is used in a proceeding to consolidate agricultural holdings.
predicates.objections_to_principles_and_proposals_a: Persons affected by proposed consolidation principles and land allocations may object and have those objections heard.
predicates.title_disputes_receive_a_hearing_and_evi: The procedure for resolving disputed land titles includes a hearing for the parties and consideration of evidence.
predicates.finality_and_stays_prevent_delay: The resolution is made final and related ordinary court proceedings are stayed to prevent delay in consolidation.
predicates.procedural_limits_advance_consolidation_: The procedural limits are reasonably connected to completing the consolidation scheme in a reasonable time.

issues.definition: When a consolidation proceeding hears objections to its principles and proposals, provides a hearing and consideration of evidence in title disputes, and uses finality and stays to prevent delay in furthering consolidation, its procedure does not violate equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: Cash compensation for a small contribution of land to common purposes is not inadequate when the contribution is small, the land is consolidated for the benefit of the tenure-holders, and they also receive the advantages of common facilities and compact holdings.
material_facts: The Act required tenure-holders to contribute small portions of land for common purposes; the contribution in the petitioners’ case was just over one-half of one percent of the relevant land value.
The contributed portions were combined with other land, including vacant land, into a larger area for purposes such as pasture, tree planting, schools, playgrounds, and community facilities.
The common area benefited the tenure-holders, who also gained the advantages of having their scattered holdings consolidated into compact blocks.
The Act provided cash compensation for land taken for those purposes, and the petitioners challenged its adequacy.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming Article 31(2), as it stood before the Fourth Amendment, applied, the cash compensation together with the benefits of the common land and compact holdings was not inadequate; the challenge failed.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing adequacy of compensation in the circumstances of a consolidation scheme, the Court considered not only cash compensation but also the direct benefits to tenure-holders from the common land and compact holdings. The Court relied on Article 31(2), section 29-B and section 14(1)(ee) of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, and the purposes specified in the applicable rules. It found it unnecessary to decide the arguments about the effect of the Fourth Amendment. No earlier judicial decisions were relied upon for this ruling.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and only_a_small_land_contribution_is_taken and contributed_land_is_combined_for_common_benefit and tenure_holders_receive_direct_consolidation_benefits and cash_compensation_is_provided

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The challenged taking occurs as part of a proceeding to consolidate agricultural holdings.
predicates.only_a_small_land_contribution_is_taken: Each tenure-holder contributes only a small portion of land for common purposes.
predicates.contributed_land_is_combined_for_common_: The contributed land is combined with other land to create a larger area used for common purposes benefiting the tenure-holders.
predicates.tenure_holders_receive_direct_consolidat: The tenure-holders receive direct benefits from the common area and from having their holdings consolidated into compact blocks.
predicates.cash_compensation_is_provided: The law provides cash compensation for the contributed land.

issues.definition: When a consolidation proceeding takes only a small land contribution, combines it for common benefit, provides cash compensation, and gives tenure-holders direct benefits from common facilities and compact holdings, the compensation is not inadequate.
